rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard DFT slab calculation with adsorption energy definitions, but it requires careful construction of multiple surface+adsorbate configurations and correct energy equations. It is an established, non-trivial method needing domain knowledge in surface chemistry and DFT.
rationale.execution: The workflow involves multiple sequential DFT calculations (slab, gas-phase, many adsorbate configurations) and post-processing to combine energies. This is a multi-stage pipeline with dependencies, but it uses a single tool (Quantum ESPRESSO) and no external data fetching beyond generating input structures.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard plane-wave DFT to a surface disproportionation reaction. Reproducing the energetics requires setting up multiple slab+adsorbate configurations, running DFT optimizations, and computing energy differences. The method is well-established but non-trivial, and the pipeline involves several dependent DFT runs and post-processing steps. Resource needs are modest: a small periodic slab (~108 atoms) can be handled on a single CPU node without GPUs.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small periodic DFT slab calculations (~108 atoms per supercell) with modest k-point mesh and moderate cutoff are feasible on a single CPU node with a few GB of memory; no GPU is required, and input data is generated in-code, so data volume is negligible.
